description: Index-based iterator interface for bounded collections. Proves the core traversal invariants (0 <= idx <= len) using only Z3 integer theory, so that std/list.mm / std/alloc.mm containers can share a common traversal contract. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/iter — verified bounded iterator'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/container/safe_queue.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only what std/core.mm and std/container/safe_queue.mm already use (checked_add, checked_sub, conditional expressions, comparisons).

atoms.name: iter_new
atoms.description: Create a fresh iterator over a bounded collection of size len. The iterator position starts at 0. Requires len >= 0 so the collection is well-formed.

atoms.name: iter_has_next
atoms.description: Return 1 when the iterator still has an element to yield (idx < len), 0 otherwise. This is the fundamental traversal guard used by for/while loops over collections.

atoms.name: iter_advance
atoms.description: Advance the iterator by one step. Preserves the invariant 0 <= idx <= len so downstream atoms can rely on the bound.

atoms.name: iter_remaining
atoms.description: Number of elements still to yield (len - idx). Used by bounded traversal optimisations and by size hints in collection adapters.

atoms.name: iter_is_done
atoms.description: Return 1 when the iterator has consumed every element (idx == len), 0 otherwise. Dual of iter_has_next, exposed as a separate atom so callers can avoid negation.
